name: Johanan
source_summary: A Judean army commander after Jerusalem's fall, Johanan son of Kareah warned the governor Gedaliah of a plot to assassinate him, then avenged the murder and rescued the captives Ishmael had taken, but ultimately defied Jeremiah's prophetic warning and led the surviving remnant of Judah down into Egypt.
family_friendly_summary: After Jerusalem was destroyed, the Babylonians left a governor named Gedaliah in charge of the Judeans who remained in the land. Johanan was an army commander who found out that a man named Ishmael was planning to assassinate Gedaliah, and he warned him -- but Gedaliah didn't believe it and was killed anyway. Johanan then chased down Ishmael, rescued the people he had captured, and became a leader of the group that was left. The people asked the prophet Jeremiah what to do next, and God's answer was to stay in the land. But Johanan and the others were afraid and disobeyed, leading everyone down to Egypt instead, taking Jeremiah with them against his will.
adult_story: After Jerusalem's fall in 586 BC, Babylon appointed Gedaliah governor over the Judeans left in the land, with Johanan son of Kareah among the army commanders who submitted to him at Mizpah (2 Kings 25:22-23). When Johanan learned that Ishmael, a member of the royal family, was plotting to assassinate Gedaliah at the instigation of the king of Ammon, he warned Gedaliah directly and even offered to kill Ishmael secretly first -- Gedaliah refused to believe it and forbade the plan (Jeremiah 40:13-16). Ishmael assassinated Gedaliah as warned, along with Judeans and Babylonian soldiers stationed there, then marched off with captives (41:1-10). Johanan pursued, intercepted Ishmael's group, and rescued the captives, though Ishmael himself escaped to Ammon (41:11-15). Fearing Babylonian reprisal for Gedaliah's murder, Johanan and the remaining leaders asked Jeremiah to seek the LORD's guidance, vowing in advance to obey whatever answer came (42:1-6). Jeremiah's answer, after ten days, was unambiguous: stay in the land, do not fear the king of Babylon, and God would build them up; going to Egypt for safety would instead bring the very sword and famine they feared (42:7-22). Johanan and the other leaders accused Jeremiah of lying and led the remnant of Judah down into Egypt anyway, forcibly taking Jeremiah and Baruch with them (43:1-7) -- a final act of unbelief that closes out the story of Judah's remnant in the historical books, disobedience compounding the very judgment it feared.

devotionals: Johanan promised to obey whatever God said, then disobeyed the very answer Jeremiah gave him. Jesus wants us to actually follow his guidance, not just ask for it.
